dedupe_keys.name: nlr geothermal supply curves us hydrothermal and enhanced geothermal system potential with levelized cost of energy and transmission

description: Supply curve data for US geothermal electricity, published with an interactive map. Contents: hydrothermal potential at 3.5 km depth, enhanced geothermal system (EGS) binary potential at 4.5 and 5.5 km and EGS flash potential at 6.5 km, with temperatures from Southern Methodist University at 2.5 km cells. The data hold levelized cost of energy and levelized cost of transmission per scenario, as CSV files with latitude, longitude, available area, capacity potential, generation potential, capacity factor and distance and cost to interconnection. The page's summary table gives developable area of 577,211 km2 and 1,642 GW for hydrothermal binary, 999,961 to 1,623,779 km2 and 3,698 to 7,018 GW for EGS binary and 701,062 km2 and 6,500 GW for EGS flash, with an exclusions table (federal lands, military lands, BLM lands, sage grouse habitat and others). Producer: NLR geospatial science. Coverage: conterminous United States. Format and access: CSV downloads and a web map; page updated 4 May 2026. Free. Licence: not stated on the page read. Caveats: scenario-based technical potential using 2035 cost assumptions. Simulation uses: geothermal siting, cost and transmission inputs for capacity expansion models. Related records: the Open Energy Data Initiative record and the NLR Siting Lab record.
